title: Shared I²C buses and BNO055
summary: Share compatible SDA/SCL pins, declare hardware addresses and use the orientation sensor controls.
body: These additions are in the development source. They are not yet a new published Windows EXE, Android APK or hardware-verified sensor release.

Sharing SDA and SCL

Devices can share the same two GPIOs when their seven-bit I²C addresses differ. Their internal register numbers may overlap. Select the same SDA and SCL pair for compatible devices; do not cross the lines or share an interrupt/reset pin. Windows and web configuration provide an I²C address selector. Match the module’s actual address straps/jumpers: this selector does not change a hardware address.

An unspecified address reserves all possible addresses of that profile. Declare the actual address when needed to resolve a potential conflict. For example, OLED at 0x3C, BNO055 at 0x28 and DS3231 at 0x68 can share a bus. An MPU6050 at 0x68 conflicts with the RTC; its hardware AD0 setting can select 0x69. PCA9685 devices need distinct unicast addresses, but may share their All Call broadcast address.

Firmware and board limits

The implemented OLED, RTC and BNO055 drivers use one matching external bus pair and serialize transactions. Built-in LCD touch keeps its own controller. Compact ESP8266/ESP8285/C2 firmware retains its existing peripheral restrictions. Catalog wiring support does not mean every expander, ADC or codec has a runtime driver. Bus pull-ups must be compatible with ESP 3.3 V signals; check any additional chips on the breakout board too.

DFRobot BNO055

  1. Add DFRobot BNO055 in Sensors on a full-feature ESP32 target.
  2. Assign SDA and SCL, optionally reusing the OLED/RTC pair. Use the matching 0x28 or 0x29 hardware address, or automatic detection.
  3. After installing matching firmware, open the compass-icon Orientation sensor tab in Windows or the web interface. Windows uses the device IP configured in Compile and flash.
  4. Read the magnetic compass, acceleration, gyro, magnetic field, roll/pitch and calibration levels. The LCD dropdown has a compact readout and the same controls.

NDOF combines compass and motion; IMU mode omits magnetic heading. Live sampling can be paused. Move the sensor through different orientations away from magnets to calibrate; level 3 is fully calibrated. Reinitialize restarts calibration. Offline or stale readings are cleared. Support covers BNO055 functions and does not assume the Gravity version’s additional BMP280 exists.
